Perennos Tempo 2.0 adds the apps: local AI tools you install on your own computer. They talk to the engines you own, ask before anything that matters, and keep your files on your machine.

## What's in it

- **Tempo Agent.** A local AI agent that reads and edits files, runs commands and reads web pages, asking first before anything that changes things. `/undo` puts its last changes back. Your own hooks can run around its steps, and long commands can run in the background (`/stop` ends them). If one of your machines is off, it moves to the next.
- **Tempo Vault.** Your notes as plain Markdown files, Obsidian-compatible. Tempo reads and links them and learns from them on your computer.
- **Tempo Studio.** Mixing and mastering: loudness, analysis and REAPER sessions.
- **Tempo Room.** A private group chat on your computer. Ask `@tempo`, and invite family or a team with a one-time key. Guests never get tools, files or your memory.
- **tempo-launch.** Starts and stops everything without a console window. `tempo-launch setup` checks the memory, graphics card and disk, recommends models that fit, and fetches them (and Ollama itself, checked against a pinned SHA-256) only after you say yes.

## Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `PerennosTempo-Setup-2.0.0-x64-source-available.exe` | Windows 10 and 11 (x64) |
| `perennos-tempo-source-available-2.0.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | macOS on Apple silicon |
| `perennos-tempo-source-available-2.0.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | Linux (x86_64) |
| `perennos-tempo-source-available_2.0.0-1_amd64.deb` | Debian and Ubuntu (x86_64) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | The SHA-256 of every file above |

**Check a download before you open it:**

- Linux: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`
- macOS: `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`
- Windows (PowerShell): `Get-FileHash .\PerennosTempo-Setup-2.0.0-x64-source-available.exe`, then compare it with the line in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
- Any system with the GitHub CLI: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo Perennos/perennos-tempo` checks that this repository's release workflow built the file.

**Install:**

- **Windows:** open the installer and follow its steps.
- **macOS and Linux:** run `tar xzf <file> && cd perennos-tempo-source-available-*/ && ./install.sh`. On Debian or Ubuntu you can use `sudo apt install ./<file>.deb` instead.

Then run `tempo-launch setup`. Nothing large is downloaded until you say yes.

**Uninstall:**

- **Windows:** use Settings, Apps. It removes the programs and keeps your vault, Tempo's memory and the logs.
- **macOS and Linux:** run `install.sh --uninstall`. It moves what it installed to a trash folder.

## Good to know

- **Unsigned files.** The Windows installer is not code-signed, so Windows may warn before it opens it. On macOS, `install.sh` signs the programs for your computer only and removes the download flag.
- **The engines.** Tempo runs your models through Ollama on your own machines. `tempo-launch setup` can fetch a pinned Ollama for you.
- **Licence.** These files are the source-available edition, under the PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 licence: free to use, change and share, for yourself or your business. The paid Tempo Field and VECTIS are not in them.
- **Your data.** Each app keeps its data in one Tempo home folder on your computer (docs/TEMPO-HOME.md). See PRIVACY.md.
